correctness.rationale: Starting from the 2023 wrapped XLindley density, the mixed angular/parameter log derivative is J=-1-b'/((t+b)^2); the sign at t=0 is governed by K(λ)=(exp(2πλ)-1)[(λ+2)^2+1]+2π(2λ+4-2π). Its derivative is strictly positive, K(0)<0, and K tends to infinity, proving a unique boundary. At the terminal angle J<0 for every positive parameter. The explicit two-parameter slope Q(t) is either everywhere negative or strictly decreases and crosses zero exactly once. All quantifiers and the fixed-origin seam are specified. Standalone Python checker passed 506 tests, including exact rational π and exponential bounds proving the cutoff enclosure and strict positive slope for parameters 0.10 and 0.11; numerical diagnostics do not replace the all-parameter argument.

value.rationale: The direct publication of a wrapped version of a likelihood-ratio-ordered family raises a natural mathematically substantive question: does strong stochastic comparison survive a many-to-one time-of-day transformation? The theorem supplies a complete sharp threshold for universal order and an exact all-parameter density-ratio shape classification. This is structurally stronger than a pointwise counterexample and has immediate NP most-powerful rejection-geometry implications (initial versus interior angular arcs) for a single observation. It does not claim unknown-location inference or multi-observation UMP performance.
